lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: For the year ended December 31, 2025, two customers accounted for more than 10% of our total consolidated revenue, with HP Risk and HPMA accounting for 23.8% and 11.3%, respectively.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, one customer accounted for more than 10% of our total consolidated revenue, with HPMA accounting for 26.1 %.

There were no major customers contributing more than 10% of revenue, aside from HPMA and HP Risk, as noted above, for the year ended December 31, 2025, and there were no major customers contributing more than 10% of revenue, aside from HPMA, as noted above, for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Within the direct channel, our sales and marketing efforts are focused on the primary sources of business referrals.

A company that falls within the scope of Section 3(a)(1)(C) of the 1940 Act can avoid being regulated as an investment company if it can rely on certain of the exclusions or exemptions under the 1940 Act.

We believe that these additional purchases allow us to rely on the safe harbor from investment company registration set forth in Rule 3a-1 of the 1940 Act because we own (i) at least 25% of the voting securities of HC Realty, resulting in us being presumed to control HC Realty within the meaning of Section 2(a)(9) of the 1940 Act and (ii) a sufficient number of shares of HC Series B Stock so that we primarily control HC Realty within the meaning of Rule 3a-1 of the 1940 Act.

We have not sought or obtained an exemptive order, no-action letter or any other assurances from the SEC or its staff regarding our ability to rely on Rule 3a-1 of the 1940 Act, nor has the SEC or its staff provided any such order, no-action letter or other assurances.
We depend on our ability to attract and retain key personnel and agents, and our inability to do so could adversely affect our business.

Our title insurance and title agency subsidiaries rely on their systems, employees and domestic banks to transfer funds on behalf of our title insurance and title agency subsidiaries as well as title agents that are not affiliates of ours.

HC Realty depends on leases by the U.S. government and its agencies for substantially all of its revenues and any failure by the U.S. government and its agencies to perform their obligations under their leases or renew their leases upon expiration could have a material adverse effect on our investment in HC Realty.
We expect that leases to agencies of the U.S. government will continue to be HC Realty’s primary source of revenues for the foreseeable future.
HC Realty’s continued qualification as a REIT depends on its satisfaction of certain asset, income, organizational, distribution and stockholder ownership requirements on a continuing basis.

HC Realty’s ability to satisfy some of the asset tests depends upon the fair market values of its assets, some of which are not able to be precisely determined and for which HC Realty has indicated it will not obtain independent appraisals.
The consolidation assessment, including the determination as to whether an entity qualifies as a VOE or VIE, depends on the facts and circumstances surrounding each entity.
